instructions: Get the T-number from .TODO/config.json before adding new tasks. Assign a stable T- prefixed task number to every active task in todo-next.md and every completed task in todo-done.md, and keep that number unchanged when moving work between active and done. Keep todo-future.md and todo-ignore.md as T-number-free retired queues; validate them with plain bullet descriptions and label suffixes instead of task IDs. Keep todo-next.md as the only active queue. Move completed tasks from todo-next.md to todo-done.md, deferred tasks to todo-future.md, and deliberate no-fix decisions to todo-ignore.md. Keep one task per bullet and store TODO metadata in .TODO/config.json. Write task descriptions as direct present-action statements and avoid retrospective phrasing such as 'now ...'. Write TODO text with super-precise, concise, goal-oriented, effect-oriented language. Avoid unnecessary file names, folder names, function names, internal IDs, or implementation details that can change; describe the required behavior and target outcome. Do not duplicate tasks that already exist in todo-next.md. Add generic labels from config.json to every task. Group TODO files by primary label using ## Label: label-name sections. Use (labels: label, label) on active, future, and ignore tasks. Use (labels: label, label; commit: shortsha) on done tasks, or commit: worktree until the work is committed. Preserve commit numbers from the actual commit that completed the task, or use commit: worktree until the task is committed.
suggestions: Keep TODO-next focused on important developer and end-user work.
Use shared config under data-config/frontend_shared.json and data-config/server.json for the date/alias rule source.
Document relative date calculation rules and deterministic overwriteToday behaviour.
Write task bullets as stable present-action statements, not retrospectives.
Write task bullets with super-precise wording that names the actor or owner when needed and states the exact current action.
Avoid task wording that begins with 'now', 'now also', 'now removed', 'now always', or similar changelog-style phrasing.
Write every text file as current-state behavior and current rules; mention past states, removed options, speculative possibilities, or future blockages only for risk prevention.
Update docs/AI-interaction after every durable AI instruction change, including user instructions, AI instructions, prompt examples, and post-interaction memory capture rules.
Keep reusable prompt examples in docs/AI-interaction/prompt-library as separate files and update its README.md as the index.
Use docs/AI-interaction/prompt-library/ai-memory-collection-post-interaction.md after each completed request/response cycle and keep only durable learning.
Use docs/AI-interaction/prompt-library/ai-memory-collection.md to convert it into durable project records.
Prefer compact status updates that state phase, action, result, and next action during long-running work.
Preserve other-agent and user worktree changes; check active work before editing or committing.
Optimize memory usage when multiple agents run at the same time; avoid starting heavy builds or typechecks unless validation requires them.
When concurrent agents may have committed, re-read relevant files and git status before final validation.
Use smart TODO state handling: active and done tasks keep stable T-numbers; future and ignore tasks stay T-number-free and still carry labels.
Use commit: worktree for completed tasks that are not committed yet, then replace it with the real short commit hash after commit.
Keep Railway test deploy reviews scoped to beta and dist-test unless the user explicitly names another branch.
Record broad audit findings as trace categories, then move actionable implementation into TODO-next and deferred risk prevention into TODO-future.
